account: Today I have heard repeated, vague reports of a bridge or port change at the bakery, but have not verified any actual change or disruption. The secretary says the baker crossed the plaza bridge safely this morning. Reports also place the innkeeper carrying sacks of bread at the bakery and market, and earlier notes mention the baker taking bread to the inn. This suggests cooperation around bread and hospitality, not necessarily anything improper. Tonight's eighteen o'clock great hall presentation is from the inn and local tradespeople, arranged with my approval yesterday. I suspect the bread movements may support hospitality or larger orders, but I do not know that firsthand. The baker now reports eight hay bales stored this morning and sixty-four loaves at his stall at fifteen nineteen, with no immediate bakery shortage. He has no confirmed delivery information and is asking whether a baking contribution is expected tonight, so I cannot assume he has been organizing the presentation. The miller's stock and delivery report remains missing because the secretary could not locate him. Separately, the accounts ledger's whereabouts and the town's obligations remain unknown; I have no evidence linking that to the bread activity. The neighbour has proposed a bench clear of the ferry approach, describing comfort rather than a known hazard. I intend to attend the presentation and hear directly what the innkeeper and tradespeople have been arranging.
